transcript:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick roll call?
[00:06] Jordan: jordan here, cto.
[00:08] Maya: maya, head of ml.
[00:10] Ethan: ethan, platform.
[00:12] Samira: and from redwood we have liam se and priya on cs.
[00:18] Liam: hey all, liam here, i'll be running the bench and technical side.
[00:22] Priya: priya will coordinate schedule and success criteria on our side.
[00:27] Samira: cool, agenda is short: align on what success looks like for the POC, what data and access we need, how we'll measure, and the timeline with milestones.
[00:34] Jordan: sounds good, we have about 6 weeks budgeted for an initial pilot.
[00:38] Samira: perfect, we'll sketch a timeline. first question — what are your must-have success criteria?
[00:44] Maya: from ml perspective accuracy is primary — we need parity with our current transformer baseline or better on our ranking/response-quality metric. also hallucination rate must be below 2% on our eval set.
[00:56] Ethan: platform cares about latency P99 under 350ms for live inference at our typical payload sizes and sustainable throughput of ~200 qps per model instance, and cost per 1k tokens to be competitive. data residency and audit logs are mandatories.
[01:12] Samira: good, that's clear. we'll capture accuracy thresholds, latency SLOs, throughput targets, and security requirements as acceptance criteria.
[01:19] Liam: technical note: for latency and throughput we'll run two benchmark modes — steady-state throughput and tail-latency spikes with small batches. we'll also run a KV cache test to mimic session-based calls.
[01:30] Maya: what about model variants? we may want an int8 quantized variant vs full fp16 to balance cost.
[01:35] Liam: yep, we can include quantized runs. redwood's runtime will pick kernels differently; expect some variance. i will document the exact hardware profile and kernel/quantization settings we use.
[01:45] Ethan: on security, we need VPC peering or private link and KMS integration — can't have customer data leaving our cloud.
[01:52] Samira: understood. for a private deployment we'll propose redwood private with customer-managed network; for the POC we can do VPC peering into a dedicated test project.
[02:01] Jordan: timeline question — what are typical milestones you run?
[02:04] Samira: standard POC timeline we use: kickoff (week 0), access & environment setup (week 1–2), initial bench & smoke tests (week 2–3), mid-point review/demo with metrics (week 3–4), optimizations and rerun (week 4–5), exec readout + decision (week 5–6).
[02:22] Maya: that aligns with our 6-week budget. can we zoom into the mid-point review — what do you expect to show?
[02:28] Liam: mid-point will include baseline benchmark numbers: throughput, P50/P95/P99 latency, token cost estimates, and accuracy on a reserved eval set. we'll highlight regressions and suggested optimizations (batching, quantization, cache profiles).
[02:40] Samira: and we'll tie that to go/no-go criteria you set — for example if P99 > 500ms or hallucination > 5% that's a red flag.
[02:48] Ethan: acceptable. also want the test harness to be repeatable so we can run it internally as well.
[02:54] Liam: i'll provide a reproducible harness (github link) and a small dockerized runner. expect to share by Friday (2026-11-14).
[03:02] Maya: for datasets, we have a representative sample — about 50k sessions, but can extract smaller slices. we'll send a 5k sample with golden outputs for the initial run.
[03:12] Samira: great — action: maya to send 5k sample by 2026-11-18.
[03:17] Ethan: network side: we need to open peering and service account. what details do you need?
[03:22] Liam: i'd need CIDR and project IDs, plus a service account with compute and storage read access for the test infra. we also prefer ephemeral keys for the POC.
[03:30] Ethan: i'll provision and share by 2026-11-20.
[03:33] Jordan: what's the benchmark hardware? we run on G4/Trn or internal GPU?
[03:37] Liam: for hosted tests we'll initially use nvidia a10g equivalent, and we can show dedicated multi-GPU runs if you want to simulate high qps. note: different GPU families change perf numbers, we'll record those.
[03:49] Maya: please also capture tokenization cost variations — our prompt lengths vary a lot.
[03:53] Liam: will do, we'll include sequence length buckets (short, medium, long) in the harness.
[03:58] Samira: can we talk about acceptance criteria and readout? jordan what does the exec team need to see to sign?
[04:03] Jordan: high-level: clear cost math showing cost per 1M tokens, demo of end-to-end latency under expected load, and a risk summary (security, support, SLAs). ideally a concise deck for the exec readout.
[04:14] Priya: priya will own the exec readout deck with samira, and we can run a dry-run with your execs a few days prior.
[04:20] Maya: what about failure modes and fallbacks? if an optimized quantized model degrades accuracy, we need auto-fallback to a higher-quality variant.
[04:28] Liam: redwood supports policy-based routing: we can demo an automatic fallback policy in the POC, route by latency or quality metric. note — demo will be synthetic for the POC but we can show the mechanic.
[04:40] Ethan: do you support auditing and SSO for the console?
[04:43] Samira: yes, console has audit logs, SAML SSO, and RBAC; for POC we'll give admin-level temporary access and demo audit traceability.
[04:51] Maya: ok good. any blockers on our side?
[04:54] Ethan: only network and SA, which we'll provide. maybe legal needs a quick NDA addendum — procurement pinged me.
[05:01] Samira: i'll loop in legal; we usually attach a short POC addendum, i'll circulate.
[05:06] Jordan: curious about competitors — can you show us how redwood differs from deepserve?
[05:10] Samira: short answer: redwood emphasizes predictable inference economics and runtime optimizations (batching, kv cache), plus unified ops across hosted/dedicated/private. we'll include a one-pager comparing to deepserve and cloudai.
[05:22] Maya: good. let's recap owners and dates.
[05:25] Samira: recap: kickoff week of 2026-11-23. liam shares benchmark repo by 2026-11-14. samira sends SOW+pricing by 2026-11-16. maya provides sample data by 2026-11-18. ethan provides network/service account by 2026-11-20. mid-point review targeted week of 2026-12-14. exec readout targeted week of 2026-12-21.
[05:48] Priya: i'll create calendar invites for kickoff and block mid-point and exec readout tentative slots.
[05:53] Jordan: that's fine. one more question on reporting — can you provide token-level cost breakdowns in the mid-point report?
[05:59] Liam: yes, we'll include token-level breakdown, CPU/GPU utilization, and per-route cost.
[06:05] Maya: and accuracy table with confusion analysis for top intents.
[06:09] Liam: added.
[06:11] Samira: any final Qs?
[06:13] Ethan: none from me.
[06:14] Jordan: no.
[06:15] Maya: no.
[06:16] Samira: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the SOW and a shared spreadsheet with the milestone tracker.
[06:22] (end)

Notes: transcript contains occasional misattributions and minor transcription errors typical of automated meeting notes (e.g., "kv cache" sometimes transcribed as "k v cash"). References shared: POC deck link: https://redwood.app/docs/cobalt-poc-deck.pdf ; benchmark repo: https://github.com/redwood/poc-harness/tree/cobalt ; security brief link: https://redwood.app/security/poc-brief.pdf

POC Milestones (text summary):
- Kickoff (week of 2026-11-23): align on goals, access kickoff, calendar invites.
- Access & environment (by 2026-11-20): VPC peering/service account, test buckets, KMS config.
- Initial benchmarks (2026-11-23 to 2026-11-30): run smoke and steady-state tests, share raw numbers.
- Mid-point review (week of 2026-12-14): demo metrics, accuracy, cost estimates, suggested optimizations.
- Optimization & rerun (2026-12-14 to 2026-12-20): tuning (batching, quantization, cache) and final runs.
- Exec readout & decision (week of 2026-12-21): concise deck, cost math, risk summary, go/no-go decision.

Acceptance Criteria (examples to be refined into SOW):
- Accuracy: model accuracy within +/-1% of current baseline on reserved eval.
- Hallucination: <2% on representative eval set.
- Latency: P99 < 350ms at target payload distribution.
- Throughput: sustain 200 qps for target load pattern with acceptable degradation.
- Security: VPC peering or private link in place, KMS encryption for keys, audit logs enabled.

End of file.
